2b5c5dfa26: 戴意誠 (1998): the three elements of the voice are breath, resonance and phonation. Breath is the power, resonance is the amplifier, and phonation decides which words the audience hears.
a9c67a6ab4: Resonance is the amplifier of your singing voice
1c7137e977: The simplest definition of resonance: an object sounding because it vibrates in sympathy.
ca05890b2f: The raw sound from the vocal folds is like a single string on its own, faint and thin. Only with the sympathetic vibration of the body's spaces does it become a ringing, sustained singing voice.
018ed44e3d: After the vote, the teacher demonstrates on guitar: the difference between holding the body and letting it go.
fd1b197591: If a guitar had only strings and no body, how would the sound change?
47132eeae9: The body is the guitar's resonating box. The strings decide the pitch, while volume and tone depend on the box amplifying them. The voice's resonating boxes are the mouth, head and chest.

5bf24d6927: Vibration felt in the head and the bridge of the noseHum /m/ with your mouth closed; the bridge of the nose and between the eyebrows tingle. The tone is soft and rich; be careful it doesn't turn into a squeezed, nasal sound.

5bc68d6d54: The shape of the mouth and pharynx shapes the toneWhen you yawn, the soft palate lifts and the back of the mouth opens. The tone is crisp and bright; be careful not to mistake "opening" for squeezing hard.

f53ff40fa0: Opening the mouth: the key is to "hold it open", not "force it open"
c5fc35920e:
Pretend to yawn and remember the "big space" at the back of your mouth: soft palate up, tongue root relaxed, jaw hanging naturally.

Keep that space and sigh gently on "ha".
d6408f8b93:
Mistaking "opening" the throat for squeezing hard: veins stand out on the neck and the sound gets stiff and stuck.

The /a/ and /o/ vowels in Taiwanese songs open wider, which makes them perfect for practising that open feeling.

b4283599e9: As resonance moves from chest to head, the frequency rises and the volume (amplitude) drops noticeably. That's normal: through the register break, bring the volume down and keep the mouth open so the two sounds hand over gradually, instead of pushing harder.

7723538041: What to adjust if it gets muffled
4bcacdb66b: Open your mouth a little more, lift the soft palate and imagine sending the sound forward from between your eyebrows rather than squeezing it out of your nostrils.
925cc3139e: Build6. Chest resonance｜Deep and solid
8f59db8c59: Put your palm on your chest and feel the low vibration
d1c1c25b1a:
Three notes below your speaking pitch, say /hei/, or say a low "mm-hmm".

When your palm feels the chest vibrate, that's chest resonance. Like telling someone what's on your mind, no force needed.
f5f29e320a:
Pressing the throat down to make a "really deep" sound.

It sounds full, but the throat is tight, high notes become hard to reach and you tire quickly.

606a2ef2de: All three resonances work together, in different proportions
4c7c7b7eee: Without the polish of head resonance the voice sounds dry and hard; without the support of chest resonance it sounds thin and floaty.
c994bf5520: Three tips for getting through the register break
ee2cc0d611:
① Bring the volume down a little
② Keep the mouth open
③ Let chest and head hand over gradually instead of pushing harder
e901e89dc3: In the high range, which resonance takes a bigger share?
64d5606d80: The high range uses more head resonance, the low range leans on the chest, and the mouth stays open all the way. Pushing high notes with chest resonance easily cracks the voice or turns into shouting.
